selection.text: The pilot plant treats river water in two stages before it reaches the storage tank. The first stage removes sand
and large particles, and the second stage removes fine particles and germs. Both stages were built from
standard parts so that the plant can be copied by small towns. The rest of this note explains the layout of each
stage and the sensors that watch it.

script.text: The pilot plant treats river water in two stages before it reaches the storage tank.
The first stage removes sand and large particles, and the second stage removes fine particles and germs.
Both stages were built from standard parts so that the plant can be copied by small towns.
The rest of this note explains the layout of each stage and the sensors that watch it.

selection.text: Water is pumped from the river through a coarse intake and a rotating screen. The settler gives heavy particles
about forty minutes to sink before the water moves on. A slow sand filter then removes most of the remaining
turbidity. The second stage adds a small dose of coagulant, which helps the membrane catch fine particles.

script.text: Water is pumped from the river through a coarse intake and a rotating screen.
The settler gives heavy particles about forty minutes to sink before the water moves on.
A slow sand filter then removes most of the remaining turbidity.
The second stage adds a small dose of coagulant, which helps the membrane catch fine particles.

selection.text: Figure 1: The two treatment stages. Stage one is shown on the left and stage two on the right.

script.text: Figure 1 shows both stages side by side.
In panel a, river water first passes the Intake.
The rotating Screen catches leaves and plastic.
Heavy particles sink in the Settler.
The Sand filter removes most of the remaining turbidity.

selection.text: Figure 1: The two treatment stages. Stage one is shown on the left and stage two on the right.

script.text: Panel b shows the second stage.
The Dosing unit adds a small amount of coagulant.
The Membrane catches the fine particles.
The UV lamp treats the water before storage.
Clean water waits in the Storage tank.
Callout 1 marks the first backwash vessel.
Callout 2 marks the second backwash vessel.

selection.text: Figure 2: Sensor drawing. Numbers mark the four sensors described in the text.

script.text: Figure 2 places the four sensors.
Callout 3 is the turbidity probe after the sand filter.
Callout 4 is the pressure gauge across the membrane.
Callout 5 measures the lamp intensity.
Callout 6 reads the level of the storage tank.

selection.text: Four sensors watch the plant, and each one is marked with a numbered callout in the sensor drawing. The
turbidity probe sits after the sand filter and is the most important single reading. A pressure gauge across the
membrane shows when the membrane needs cleaning. The other two sensors measure the lamp intensity and
the level of the storage tank.

selection.text: Alarm limits were set conservatively for the first season and will be relaxed once more data is available. Every
alarm sends a text message to the operator on duty and is written to the plant log. During the pilot the turbidity
alarm fired six times, always after heavy rain upstream.
